info.name: Credit Bladi — Simulation Scenarios
info.description:
Moroccan Mortgage Credit Simulator — BAM Compliant

**Folder convention (mirrors bff-customer-connector feature files):**
- `resource` → nominal / happy-path requests
- `resourceAccesses` → access restriction scenarios (401, 403)
- `resourceErrors` → validation & business-rule errors (400, 404, 409, 422, 415)

**Auth model:** login/register/refresh set two HttpOnly cookies (`cb_access_token`, `cb_refresh_token`) — the JWT is never returned in the response body. Postman's cookie jar auto-captures them, but since the collection needs to hold a CLIENT session and a MANAGER session at the same time, each login test script also copies the cookie value into a collection variable (`client_access_token` / `manager_access_token`); protected requests attach it manually via an explicit `Cookie` header.

**Run with the `dev` Spring profile** (`security.cookie.secure=false`) when testing over plain `http://localhost:8080` — the `Secure` cookie attribute is otherwise set and browsers/clients depending on it may not persist the cookie over non-TLS.

**Quick start:**
1. `auth / 1. Register CLIENT` → 201
2. `auth / 2. Login CLIENT` → cookies captured into `client_access_token` / `client_refresh_token`
3. `auth / 3. Login MANAGER` → cookies captured into `manager_access_token` / `manager_refresh_token`
4. All protected folders reference `{{manager_access_token}}` / `{{client_access_token}}` via an explicit `Cookie` header

CSP codes: FONC | SALA | RETR | PROF | INDE — all five now have active seeded credit-rate rows.
Amount: 70 000–30 000 000 MAD | Duration: 12–300 months (also bounded per-CSP by the credit-rate record) | Property value: 80 000–50 000 000 MAD | Monthly income: 1 000–5 000 000 MAD | Age: 18–74.

**Rate limits** (per client IP, see `RateLimitFilter`): login/register 5 req/window, refresh 10, logout 10, simulation 20. This collection stays under those ceilings for a single top-to-bottom run; re-running it quickly (e.g. via Collection Runner) may need a short pause first.

item.name: 9. POST /refresh — reused (already-rotated) token → 401  (revokes ALL client sessions)

request.description:
Replays the refresh token captured right before `auth / 6. POST /refresh` rotated it — refresh tokens are single-use, so replaying the old one is treated as theft (REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED) and revokes every refresh token for that user, including the current valid one.

Run `auth / 6. POST /refresh` first. **Run this LAST in authErrors** — it invalidates `{{client_refresh_token}}` as a side effect.

**Expected:** `401 Unauthorized`

exec: pm.test('401 - Refresh token reuse detected', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: authAccountLockout
item.description: ⚠️ RUN IN ISOLATION ONLY — not part of the standard top-to-bottom flow. `LoginAttemptStore` locks an account (423) after 5 failed logins for the SAME username, but `RateLimitFilter` also caps `/api/v1/auth/login` at 5 requests per 60s PER CLIENT IP (shared across every username). Running this folder back-to-back with `auth`/`authErrors` in the same 60s window means the 3 earlier login calls already consumed part of that budget, and this folder's 5 attempts will likely hit 429 before reaching the lockout threshold. To exercise this scenario reliably: wait 60+ seconds after the last `/api/v1/auth/login` call above (or run this folder alone via 'Run folder' in a fresh 60s window).

item.name: 1. Register throwaway account for lockout test → 201

request.description:
Dedicated username so this folder doesn't lock out `client.demo1` used everywhere else.

**Expected:** `201 Created` (or `409` if this folder already ran once — either way, proceed).

`security.login-lockout.max-attempts` defaults to 5. Send this exact request 5 times in a row (use Postman's 'Run' with 5 iterations, or click Send 5 times) — the 5th failure locks the account.

**Expected:** `401 Unauthorized` on each of the first 5 calls.

Run only after 5 consecutive failures above. The lockout is enforced BEFORE credentials are even checked, so this fails even with the correct password.

**Expected:** `423 Locked` — cleared automatically after `security.login-lockout.duration-ms` (15 min default).

item.name: UC-05 — BAM Business Rules (422 Unprocessable Entity)
422 — FONC | duration 241 > RETR/FONC-independent CSP max — DURATION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

request.description:
RETR's credit-rate row caps maxDurationMonths at 240 (see changeset 002) — 241 exceeds it.

**Expected:** `422` — DURATION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

550000 / 580000 ≈ 94.8% > 90% BAM max LTV (10% minimum deposit rule).

**Expected:** `422` — DEPOSIT_INSUFFICIENT

Minimum allowed income (1 000 MAD) against a 500 000 MAD loan — all-in monthly payment far exceeds 40% of income.

**Expected:** `422` — DEBT_RATIO_EXCEEDED

age (60) + duration in years (20) = 80 > maxAgeAtMaturity (75, applies to every CSP since changeset 021).

**Expected:** `422` — AGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

request.description: Public — permitAll in SecurityConfig.
Public — explicitly permitAll alongside /actuator/health in SecurityConfig, ahead of the catch-all `/actuator/**` → hasRole(MANAGER) rule.

`metrics` is exposed (`management.endpoints.web.exposure.include`) but falls under the `/actuator/**` → hasRole(MANAGER) catch-all rule in SecurityConfig — distinct from `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/info` which are explicitly permitAll.

request.description: **Expected:** `200 OK` with a MANAGER session.

Configured via `springdoc.swagger-ui.path` (application.properties) — NOT the springdoc default `/swagger-ui.html`. Requires MANAGER unless `swagger.public=true`. springdoc typically redirects this URL to its index page, hence the broader status check.

`ApiExceptionHandler.handleNoResourceFound` maps `NoResourceFoundException` to `HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND` — verified directly against the handler source.
